units.en: ⟦0⟧, short for ⟦1⟧, is a mechanic in Hearts of Iron 4 through which nations can try to observe what other nations are doing. It can be found in the Intel Ledger. At lower intel levels, this includes seeing how many factories other nations have, what they are producing with their ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧, what ⟦4⟧ they have researched, what ⟦5⟧ they have chosen, and what equipment types they have in stockpile. At higher intel levels, nations can even get information about the exact equipment ⟦6⟧ and designs being used and the specific ⟦7⟧ and ⟦8⟧ the target country is performing. Intel can also provide bonuses in ⟦9⟧, for ⟦10⟧ and evading enemy ships, and for reducing the effectiveness of enemy naval mines, as well as detecting enemy ⟦11⟧.
With ⟦0⟧, the mechanic is greatly expanded upon, incorporating upgrades from ⟦1⟧, as well as ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ performed by ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧ done by ⟦6⟧.

Intel is particularly important in multiplayer, where otherwise somewhat predictable AI opponents are replaced with potentially very unpredictable human ones. Intel serves as one of the main ways with which to deal with that unpredictability, observing what other players are doing and anticipating what will be needed to fight them while it is early enough to make such decisions. Denying enemy intel has similarly elevated importance in multiplayer: while AI opponents cannot predict or anticipate a player's moves, human opponents can, so preventing them from seeing what you are doing until it is too late for them to prepare appropriate countermeasures can be crucial to long-term strategy.

There are four types of intel: civilian intel, army intel, navy intel, and air intel. The amount of intel that each country has on each other country is tracked individually for these four categories. Each type of intel can be gained through different sources, and higher levels in each intel type provide both different passive information about the target country to its observer and potential bonuses (or penalties) for the observer country against the target country.

⟦0⟧ covers intelligence related to a country's ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧, and ⟦6⟧, as well as its ⟦7⟧ and ⟦8⟧ technologies. The information provided by civilian intel can be especially important in the pre-war build-up phase to help anticipate what future enemies might be planning to do and prepare appropriately. Civilian intel does not provide any direct bonuses, only information.

⟦0⟧ covers intelligence related to a country's ⟦1⟧, special forces, stockpiled ⟦2⟧ (including ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧), ⟦5⟧, and army-related ⟦6⟧ spirits, as well as its ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, and ⟦10⟧. In ⟦11⟧, the side with more army intel over the other receives a bonus to its combat stats.

⟦0⟧ covers intelligence related to a country's ⟦1⟧ (including ⟦2⟧), ⟦3⟧, active ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧, and navy-related ⟦6⟧ spirits, as well as its ⟦7⟧ and ⟦8⟧. Having low navy intel against an enemy confers a penalty to contesting ⟦9⟧ against them.

⟦0⟧, also known as ⟦1⟧, covers intelligence related to a country's ⟦2⟧ (including ⟦3⟧), ⟦4⟧, active ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧, and air-related ⟦7⟧ spirits, as well as its ⟦8⟧. Should the target country plan or launch a ⟦9⟧ against the observer country, the latter will be notified of it earlier at higher levels of air intel.

The intel ledger is the place where intel levels on a country can be checked, as well as the main place where information based on gathered intel can be viewed. It can be found by opening up the diplomacy menu of another country, then selecting the tab labelled ⟦0⟧ next to the one labelled ⟦1⟧.

At the top of the intel ledger are four buttons, each corresponding to one of the four intel types. Within each of these buttons is a percentage. This represents the intel level that the current country has on the target country in the associated intel type. Hover over one of these buttons will display a tooltip showing all intel sources that contribute to the total intel level on the target country. Selecting either of these four buttons will open up a screen showing detailed information related to that intel type; yellow chevrons on the left- and right-hand sides of a button communicate that the currently opened information is related to the indicated intel type.

Generally speaking, more information will become available in the intel ledger at higher intel levels, and existing information will also become more precise at higher intel levels. For more details, consult the dedicated effects sections for ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧.

Civilian intel is generally focused on a country's economy, giving a lot of information in a broad range of topics, but providing no other bonuses besides this information. It can range between ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧.⟦2⟧

Additionally, fighting an enemy country's ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ can temporarily provide additional civilian intel. The base intel gain rate is ⟦2⟧ per ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ per day, though this is further modified by a dynamic gain rate and decay rate given to all intel gained from ⟦5⟧; see the dedicated ⟦6⟧ section for more details about these. The maximum effective cap on civilian intel gained in this way is ⟦7⟧,⟦8⟧ and the maximum hard cap on civilian intel gained in this way is ⟦9⟧.⟦10⟧ The hard cap does not contribute directly to a country's civilian intel, but intel gained within it can act as a buffer that absorbs intel decay before it can affect a country's effective civilian intel.

Certain ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ can reduce the amount of civilian intel given to other countries or increase the amount of civilian intel gained from other countries. Notably, the ⟦2⟧ spirit for ⟦3⟧ and the ⟦4⟧ decision for the ⟦5⟧ unlocked by ⟦6⟧ can lower the amount of civilian intel given to other countries significantly.
⟦0⟧ can provide civilian intel based on their levels and overall coverage. See the dedicated ⟦1⟧ section for more details.

⟦0⟧ unlocks many more potential sources for civilian intel, both from ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧. See the dedicated ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ sections for more details. Without ⟦5⟧, countries can receive additional civilian intel based on their decryption level relative to target countries' encryption levels. See the dedicated ⟦6⟧ section for more details.

Finally, when in a ⟦0⟧ with an ally who has more civilian intel on a target country, the observing country receives ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧ of the difference between them and their ally as bonus civilian intel against the target country.

Civilian intel provides information that is observable from the civilian intel tab of the intel ledger. Some types of information have binary civilian intel requirements: either the country has enough civilian intel over a target to see them, or they don't. Other types of information have more gradation: a country must have enough civilian intel over the target to see them, but the information starts out very fuzzy and becomes more precise with more civilian intel.
